screeningSummary: Plane-spotter with three years of tracking data saw something her app says wasn't there - 'is that evidence?'
arcNotes: Question arc, info-heavy: ADS-B only sees transponders (military dark, low coverage), so absence rules out scheduled traffic but proves nothing positive. Vern reframes: she shrank the sky. Next step: cross-reference her own database

lines.text: Then here's what your app told you, and what it didn't. Those trackers don't see the sky - they see transponders. A plane broadcasts its position and the app shows it. Three blind spots: military aircraft flying dark, anything below the receivers' horizon, and anything without a transponder at all. At tree-line height, your app showing nothing is the app working exactly as designed. But - and this is what your three years of data bought you - nothing at 9:15 also rules out every scheduled flight in the valley. Your hobby didn't confirm the mystery. It shrank the sky. That's more than most witnesses ever get.

lines.text: Interpretation of your data: tracking applications display transponder broadcasts - ADS-B positions - not raw sky. Three exclusion zones exist: military emissions control, sub-horizon coverage, and non-transponder-equipped craft. At tree-line altitude, an empty display reflects nominal app behavior. However, your longitudinal dataset yields a positive result: nil traffic at 21:15 excludes all scheduled aviation in the valley. Your hobby did not confirm the anomaly - it eliminated alternatives. That is a stronger evidentiary position than most witnesses achieve.

lines.text: Then your eyes and your app both did their jobs, and there's one move left: cross-reference. You have three years of data - find every night the bearing matched your ridge and the app said empty. If it's a pattern, the pattern IS the report, and a woman with a spreadsheet and a bearing is the witness investigators dream about. Log every match: date, time, bearing, duration, weather. And when the file's thick - patterns get thick, they do that - you take it to a field investigator, not a forum. Forums will ask if you're okay. Investigators will ask for the spreadsheet.
